title: Selective strain tuning of nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics in BiFeO$_\text3$
authors: Chenhang Xu, Patrick Liu, Bo Zhang, Minyong Han, Henry G. Bell, Cameron J. R. Duncan, Yusong Liu, Patrick L. Kramer, Randy Lemons, Jake D. Koralek, Alexander H. Reid, Dong Qian, Harold Y. Hwang, Alfred Zong
abstract: Quantum materials are characterized by intertwined orders, and a fundamental goal in condensed matter physics is to achieve their selective control in such a way that one order parameter can be tuned while leaving others largely unaffected. Although significant progress has been made in thermal equilibrium, realizing such control out of equilibrium remains highly challenging. Here we employed \textit{in situ} tensile strain to selectively manipulate the photoinduced lattice dynamics associated with ferroelectric and magnetic orders in multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. By applying MeV ultrafast electron diffraction to freestanding BiFeO$_3$ membranes under tunable strain, we showed that tensile strain markedly suppresses the ultrafast photoinduced reduction of the ferroelectric displacement. By contrast, the photoinduced dynamics of the antiferrodistortive rotation of the oxygen octahedra, which modulates the magnetic order, remains insensitive to strain. Not only do these findings reveal distinct microscopic pathways underlying nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics, they also establish tunable strain as an effective route for engineering ultrafast phase control in correlated materials.
summary: This work demonstrates the ability to selectively control the ultrafast dynamics of coupled ferroelectric and magnetic orders in $	ext{BiFeO}_3$ by applying tensile strain. Using ultrafast electron diffraction, the researchers showed that strain specifically dampens the ferroelectric response without affecting the magnetic (AFD) response. This establishes strain as a powerful tool for engineering non-equilibrium phase control in correlated multiferroics.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving selective, non-equilibrium control over multiple coupled order parameters (like ferroelectric and magnetic) in quantum multiferroic materials.
main_result: Tensile strain selectively suppresses the ultrafast photoinduced dynamics associated with the ferroelectric order parameter, while leaving the dynamics related to the magnetic order parameter largely unaffected.
method: The study uses *in situ* tensile strain tuning applied to freestanding $	ext{BiFeO}_3$ membranes, probed by MeV ultrafast electron diffraction following photoexcitation.
model_or_system: The system is the multiferroic $	ext{BiFeO}_3$, which exhibits coupled ferroelectric (FE) and antiferrodistortive (AFD) orders. The experiment probes the ultrafast lattice dynamics associated with these two distinct order parameters.
key_observables: Photoinduced lattice dynamics, specifically the time evolution of FE displacement and AFD rotation, measured via changes in Bragg peak intensities ($\overline{I}_{	ext{odd}} - \overline{I}_{	ext{even}}$).
important_parameters: Tunable uniaxial tensile strain ($\sim 0.2\%$), ultrafast time scales (sub-picosecond), and varying pump laser fluences.
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between structural changes (FE/AFD reduction) and transient lattice heating (Debye-Waller effect).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the comparison of measured intensity changes against simple Debye-Waller scaling, and the time evolution of FE and AFD dynamics under varying strain and fluence.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental platform, presents measurements showing the differential strain response of FE vs. AFD dynamics, and uses modeling (Ginzburg-Landau) to attribute the selective tuning to strain-mediated changes in carrier screening effects.
why_interesting: The selective control demonstrated here—tuning one order parameter while preserving another—is a key concept in designing quantum materials for advanced applications, relevant to understanding coupled dynamics in complex quantum systems.
